sections.title: Validate
paragraphs: Before you render, `validate()` returns structured CK codes with JSON Pointers. Agents loop locally — no model round-trip required for most fixes.
For agents

Point at `llms.txt`, emit a spec, then `validate()`. On failure, `repair()` applies JSON Patch locally — lifting first-try failures without another model call. Then `render()` (or SSR `renderToString`).

sections.title: Install
paragraphs: Pull the React adapter. It depends on `@chartkitdev/core` (zero runtime deps) and peers React 18+. The same spec works in Vue, Svelte, vanilla, or Node SVG.
Migrating from v0.4? Swap `@derpdaderp/chartkit` for `@chartkitdev/react`. Component props still work; prefer `<Chart spec={…} />` for new code. See migrate notes.
code: `npm i @chartkitdev/react`

sections.title: <Chart />
paragraphs: Import `Chart` from `@chartkitdev/react`. Pass a v1 `ChartSpec` — `version`, `type`, `data`, `encoding`, and required `a11y.alt`. Defaults to every chart via `@chartkitdev/core/all`.
code: `import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/react"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; const spec: ChartSpec = { version: "1", type: "line", data: [ { week: "W1", signups: 18 }, { week: "W2", signups: 28 }, { week: "W3", signups: 24 }, { week: "W4", signups: 42 }, { week: "W5", signups: 38 }, { week: "W6", signups: 56 }, { week: "W7", signups: 62 }, { week: "W8", signups: 86 } ], encoding: { x: "week", y: "signups" }, theme: "soft", a11y: { alt: "Weekly signups rose from 18 to 86." } }; export function Panel() { return <Chart spec={spec} />; }`

sections.title: Next.js App Router
paragraphs: The React package build starts with `"use client"`, so importing `Chart` (or `LineChart`) from a Server Component pulls it into the client boundary. That is the right path for hydration and interact.
Honest split: `<Chart />` is the client adapter. Static email/PDF/RSC first paint uses core `render()` (or vanilla `renderToString`). Same spec either way — that is the switch pitch.
list: Client chart — put `<Chart />` in a file with `"use client"`, or nest it under a client parent.
RSC SSR SVG — call `render()` from `@chartkitdev/core/all` in a Server Component and inject the SVG string. No React chart runtime on the wire.
code: `// app/dashboard/chart.tsx — Server Component (no "use client") import { render } from "@chartkitdev/core/all"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; const spec: ChartSpec = { /* same v1 spec */ }; export function ServerChart() { const svg = render(spec); return ( <div role="img" aria-label={spec.a11y.alt} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svg }} /> ); }`

sections.title: TypeScript
paragraphs: `ChartSpec` comes from `@chartkitdev/core` (generated from `chartkit.schema.json`). `ChartProps` accepts `spec`, optional `className` / `style`, and optional `render` for a slim bundle. Autocomplete covers every leaf the schema knows.

sections.title: Slim bundle
paragraphs: Default `<Chart />` ships every chart. Pass `render` from `createRenderer([line])` when a page only needs one type. Budgets from `size-budget.json`: core line 8.8 KB gzip, core all 20.9 KB gzip (React + framework external).

Caveat (product): the slim `createRenderer([line])` path may omit axis extras unless mounted — titles/ticks can silently no-op. Prefer `core/all` until bundles docs spell the opt-in. Mock notes the honesty gap from PLAN Decision 1.
code: `import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/react"; import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { line } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/line"; const render = createRenderer([line]); export function SlimLine({ spec }) { return <Chart spec={spec} render={render} />; }`

sections.title: Component API (still supported)
paragraphs: Dashboard components (`LineChart`, `KpiCard`, …) keep their props. `theme` is required on those; on a JSON spec it defaults to `auto`. Prop keys like `dataKey` are not spec keys — agents should emit the v1 JSON.
For agents
Emit v1 JSON (`a11y.alt` required). Validate with `@chartkitdev/core/validate`. Render with `<Chart />` or core `render()`. Point models at `llms.txt` — not at JSX prop tables.
code: `import { LineChart } from "@chartkitdev/react"; <LineChart data={rows} dataKey="signups" theme="midnight" responsive />`

sections.title: <Chart />
paragraphs: Import `Chart` from `@chartkitdev/vue`. Bind a v1 `ChartSpec` with `:spec` — `version`, `type`, `data`, `encoding`, and required `a11y.alt`. Defaults to every chart via `@chartkitdev/core/all`. Spec changes recompute the SVG string and replace the element HTML; unmount drops the node.
code: `<script setup lang="ts"> import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/vue"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; const spec: ChartSpec = { version: "1", type: "line", data: [ { week: "W1", signups: 18 }, { week: "W2", signups: 28 }, { week: "W3", signups: 24 }, { week: "W4", signups: 42 }, { week: "W5", signups: 38 }, { week: "W6", signups: 56 }, { week: "W7", signups: 62 }, { week: "W8", signups: 86 } ], encoding: { x: "week", y: "signups" }, theme: "soft", a11y: { alt: "Weekly signups rose from 18 to 86." } }; </script> <template> <Chart :spec="spec" class="panel-chart" /> </template>`

sections.title: Nuxt
paragraphs: Unlike the React adapter (which starts with `"use client"`), the Vue `Chart` draws during render — Nuxt SSR and `vue/server-renderer` include the SVG in the first HTML. Two paths:

Honest split: client and Nuxt SSR both use the same `<Chart />`. Reach for `@chartkitdev/vue/ssr` when you need a string; for pure SVG without the Vue wrapper, core `render()` still works. Same JSON either way — that is the switch pitch.
list: SFC in a page / layout — drop `<Chart :spec />` in a `.vue` component. Universal by default.
String SSR — `renderToString` from `@chartkitdev/vue/ssr` in a Nitro handler or server utility when you need the HTML string (email, edge, agent tool).
code: `<!-- components/PanelChart.vue — works in Nuxt pages & layouts --> <script setup lang="ts"> import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/vue"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; const props = defineProps<{ spec: ChartSpec }>(); </script> <template> <Chart :spec="spec" /> </template>`

`// server/api/chart.get.ts — or any Nitro handler import { renderToString } from "@chartkitdev/vue/ssr"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; export default defineEventHandler(async () => { const spec: ChartSpec = { /* same v1 spec */ }; const html = await renderToString(spec); return html; // wrapper div + core SVG string inside });`

sections.title: renderToString
paragraphs: The `./ssr` entry wraps `createSSRApp` + `vue/server-renderer`. Returns a Promise of HTML; the SVG inside is what core would emit.
code: `import { renderToString } from "@chartkitdev/vue/ssr"; const html = await renderToString(spec); // optional slim: await renderToString(spec, createRenderer([line]))`

sections.title: TypeScript
paragraphs: `ChartSpec` comes from `@chartkitdev/core` (generated from `chartkit.schema.json`). `ChartProps` accepts required `spec` and optional `render` for a slim bundle. Attrs (class, style, aria-*) fall through onto the wrapper `div` via `inheritAttrs: false` + spread.

sections.title: Slim bundle
paragraphs: Default `<Chart />` ships every chart. Pass `:render` from `createRenderer([line])` when a page only needs one type. Budgets from `size-budget.json`: Vue adapter 274 B gzip (framework external), core line 8.8 KB, core all 20.9 KB.

Caveat (product): the slim `createRenderer([line])` path may omit axis extras unless mounted — titles/ticks can silently no-op. Prefer `core/all` until bundles docs spell the opt-in. Mock notes the honesty gap from PLAN Decision 1.
code: `<script setup lang="ts"> import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/vue"; import { createRenderer } from "@chartkitdev/core"; import { line } from "@chartkitdev/core/charts/line"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; const render = createRenderer([line]); defineProps<{ spec: ChartSpec }>(); </script> <template> <Chart :spec="spec" :render="render" /> </template>`

sections.title: Reactivity
paragraphs: Pass a reactive `spec` (ref / reactive / computed). The component’s computed SVG tracks it — no imperative `update()` call. That mirrors vanilla’s `mount().update()` without exposing the handle. For agents emitting static JSON, treat the object as immutable and replace the whole spec.
For agents

Emit v1 JSON (`a11y.alt` required). Validate with `@chartkitdev/core/validate`. Render with `<Chart :spec />`, `vue/ssr` `renderToString`, or core `render()`. Point models at `llms.txt` — not at Vue prop tables.

Server load — fetch or build the v1 JSON in `+page.server.ts`, pass it as `data.spec`. Agents can emit that JSON anywhere.
code: `<!-- src/routes/dashboard/+page.svelte --> <script lang="ts"> import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/svelte"; import type { ChartSpec } from "@chartkitdev/core"; export let data: { spec: ChartSpec }; </script> <Chart spec={data.spec} />`

sections.title: `mount()`
paragraphs: Import `mount` from `@chartkitdev/vanilla`. Pass an element you already own and a v1 `ChartSpec` — `version`, `type`, `data`, `encoding`, required `a11y.alt`. Defaults to every chart via `@chartkitdev/core/all`. Returns `{ update(spec), destroy() }`. No wrapper node is inserted; SVG is written to `el.innerHTML`. Matching SVG skips the DOM write.
code: `import { mount } from "@chartkitdev/vanilla"; const spec = { version: "1", type: "line", data: [ { week: "W1", signups: 18 }, { week: "W2", signups: 28 }, { week: "W3", signups: 24 }, { week: "W4", signups: 42 }, { week: "W5", signups: 38 }, { week: "W6", signups: 56 }, { week: "W7", signups: 62 }, { week: "W8", signups: 86 } ], encoding: { x: "week", y: "signups" }, theme: "soft", a11y: { alt: "Weekly signups rose from 18 to 86." } }; const chart = mount(document.querySelector("#chart"), spec); chart.update(nextSpec); chart.destroy();`

mock-plausible: jsDelivr `+esm` paths follow the published `0.5.0` package shape; pin the version in production. Subpath `core/all` must resolve to the built file your bundler or CDN exposes.

sections.title: API
paragraphs: For agents

Emit v1 JSON (`a11y.alt` required). Validate with `@chartkitdev/core/validate`. Render with `mount(el, spec)`, `renderToString(spec)`, or core `render()`. Point models at `llms.txt` — not at framework prop tables.
list: `mount(el, spec, options?)` → `MountedChart` — draws into `el`; optional `options.render`.
`chart.update(spec)` — redraw; no-op after `destroy`; skips write when SVG matches.
`chart.destroy()` — clears `innerHTML`; further updates do nothing.
`renderToString(spec, render?)` → SVG string; default render is `core/all`.

`render(spec)` does not emit `ck-chart-error`; SVG includes `data-ck-type`.
One example per core chart type in `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, and the core README (enforced by `docs-spec.test.ts`).
`a11y.alt` required, 10–500 characters.

title: Spec anatomy
lede: A ChartKit chart is one JSON object — schema `https://chartkit.dev/schema/v1.json`. Required: `version`, `type`, `a11y`. Most charts also need `data` + `encoding`. Everything else (`mark`, `axes`, `theme`, …) has defaults. Same object in React, Vue, Svelte, vanilla, Markdown, and Node SVG.
description: A ChartKit chart is one JSON object — schema `https://chartkit.dev/schema/v1.json`. Required: `version`, `type`, `a11y`. Most charts also need `data` + `encoding`. Everything else
tryIntro: Edit the JSON or use the rail — Type / Theme focus different layers of the anatomy. The response path names which top-level keys the current view emphasizes.

sections.title: Top-level map
paragraphs: From `chartkit.schema.json` — every key a v1 spec may carry. Status notes what Concepts pages cover next.
code: `$schema optional const URL version "1" required type line | bar | donut | … required (14 core enums) id string title string subtitle string data row[] | number[] | columns usually required by type encoding x, y, series, color, size, usually required by type open, high, low, close, volume metric value, min, max, … gauge · kpi · progress-ring mark curve, sampling, stack, … options object — not the type axes x · y · y2 legend boolean | { show, position, … } tooltip boolean | { show, mode, … } annotations rule | band | text[] theme preset string | { preset, mode, tokens } size width, height, padding, … interaction hover, zoom, pan, brush, … animation boolean | { duration, easing } locale string a11y { alt } required (alt 10–500 chars)`

sections.title: Required & by-type
paragraphs: Field types on channels are `quantitative`, `temporal`, `ordinal`, or `nominal` — never `categorical` (repairs to nominal as CK1007).
list: Always — `version`, `type`, `a11y.alt`.

Series charts (line, bar, donut, stacked-area, scatter, combo, heatmap, sparkline, mini-area, spike, candlestick) — `data`. Line/bar/donut/stacked-area/combo also require `encoding.x` + `encoding.y`. Scatter needs `x`+`y`. Heatmap needs `x`+`color`.
Metric charts (gauge, kpi, progress-ring) — `metric.value` (not top-level `value`).
Candlestick — `encoding.open`, `high`, `low`, `close` (optional `volume`).

sections.title: Layers that draw
paragraphs: Think in four layers. Later Concepts pages go deep on each.
list: Identity — `version`, `type`, `id`, `title`, `subtitle`.
Data & channels — `data` (rows, number array, or `data.columns`) + `encoding` (+ `metric` when needed).
Marks & layout — `mark` (curve, sampling, stack, orientation, …), `axes`, `size`, `legend`.
Chrome & runtime — `theme`, `tooltip`, `annotations`, `interaction`, `animation`, `a11y`. Some keys validate today but only draw with `core/interact` or warn CK3012 — see Bundles.

sections.title: Richer example
paragraphs: Same line with mark, axes, theme, and size filled in. Defaults would look fine without them — this is explicit authoring.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "title": "Weekly signups", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }, { "week": "W2", "signups": 28 }, { "week": "W3", "signups": 24 }, { "week": "W4", "signups": 42 }, { "week": "W5", "signups": 38 }, { "week": "W6", "signups": 56 }, { "week": "W7", "signups": 62 }, { "week": "W8", "signups": 86 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "signups" }, "mark": { "curve": "monotone", "area": true, "sampling": "auto" }, "axes": { "x": { "title": "Week" }, "y": { "title": "Signups", "grid": true } }, "theme": "soft", "size": { "height": 280 }, "legend": false, "a11y": { "alt": "Weekly signups rose from 18 to 86." } }`

sections.title: What is not the type
list: `mark` is an options object (`curve`, `sampling`, …), not `"line"`. A string `mark` is a CK1009 repair.
`encoding.y.axis` is `"y"` or `"y2"`, not a title object — titles live under `axes.y.title`.
Aliases like `type: "pie"` → `donut`, `"area"` → `stacked-area` / `mini-area`, `"point"` → `scatter` (CK1005).
React component props are a separate API. Agents writing JSON should ignore JSX tables and use this schema.

sections.title: Machine block
paragraphs: Rendered docs pages carry the live spec next to the SVG as `<script type="application/json" data-ck-spec>`. Option pages add `id="ck-option"`. Prefer those blocks (and `.md` twins) over scraping prose.
For agents
Start from the minimal shape. Set `type` from the 14-core enum. Put measures in `encoding` or `metric`, never invent top-level `value`. Run `validate()` → `repair()` before `render()`.

sections.title: Next
paragraphs: Go deep on Data (rows vs `data.columns`), then Encoding & channels. Chart-type pages show a minimal spec per type.

title: Data
lede: `data` is what you plot — a plain array of row objects, not `{ "values": [...] }`. Sparkline, mini-area, and spike also accept a number array. For large series, prefer columnar `{ "columns": { "field": [...] } }`. Field names in `encoding` must match keys (or column names).
description: `data` is what you plot — a plain array of row objects, not `{ "values": [...] }`. Sparkline, mini-area, and spike also accept a number array. For large series, prefer columnar `{

sections.title: Rows (default)
paragraphs: One object per record. Keys are field names; values are numbers, strings (ISO 8601 on temporal fields), booleans, or `null` (missing). This is the shape in every Start example and in `llms.txt`.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }, { "week": "W2", "signups": 28 }, { "week": "W3", "signups": 24 }, { "week": "W4", "signups": 42 }, { "week": "W5", "signups": 38 }, { "week": "W6", "signups": 56 }, { "week": "W7", "signups": 62 }, { "week": "W8", "signups": 86 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "signups" }, "theme": "soft", "a11y": { "alt": "Weekly signups rose from 18 to 86." } }`

sections.title: Try a shape
paragraphs: Edit the JSON or flip Type / Theme / Shape (rows · columns · numbers). The response path shows which `$defs/data` branch you are on. Numbers only apply to sparkline / mini-area / spike — other types stay on rows in this mock.

sections.title: `data.columns`
paragraphs: Columnar form: equal-length arrays keyed by field name. Preferred for 10k+ points. In JS, arrays may be typed arrays (`Float64Array`). Encoding still names fields the same way — `encoding.x: "week"` reads `data.columns.week`.
Same chart: rows and columns above are equivalent for this line. Pick columns when agents or ETL already emit field→array maps, or when you want to avoid object-per-row overhead.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": { "columns": { "week": ["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4", "W5", "W6", "W7", "W8"], "signups": [18, 28, 24, 42, 38, 56, 62, 86] } }, "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "signups" }, "theme": "soft", "a11y": { "alt": "Weekly signups rose from 18 to 86." } }`

sections.title: Number array
paragraphs: Sparkline, mini-area, and spike may use a plain `number | null` array. The implicit field is `value`; x is the index. Other chart types require row objects or columns.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "sparkline", "data": [18, 28, 24, 42, 38, 56, 62, 86], "a11y": { "alt": "Signups rose across eight weeks." } }`

sections.title: Not `data.values`
paragraphs: Vega-style `{ "data": { "values": [...] } }` is invalid. `validate` reports CK1009; `repair()` moves `values` up so `data` is the array. Do not look for a `columns` key inside that repair — it is specifically the values unwrap.
code: `// invalid { "data": { "values": [{ "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }] } } // repaired { "data": [{ "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }] }`

sections.title: Nulls & order
list: `null` is a missing point — drawn as a gap unless `mark.connectNulls: true`.
Sampling and path drawing assume each series is already ordered by x.
Axis extents use every finite value before sampling (see Spec / Marks).
Cell types: number, string, boolean, null — no nested objects in a cell.

sections.title: Metric charts
paragraphs: Gauge, kpi, and progress-ring put the number in `metric: { value, min?, max?, delta?, label? }` — not top-level `value`. A one-row `data` table used as a sparkline beside a KPI can stay; a `data` object of metric fields is repaired into `metric` (CK1009).
For agents
Default to a row array. Use `data.columns` for wide/long columnar payloads. Never wrap rows in `values`. Match `encoding` field names to keys. Then `validate()`.

sections.title: Next
paragraphs: Encoding binds fields to channels (`x`, `y`, `color`, …). Scales and axes sit on top of those channels.

title: Encoding
lede: `encoding` binds data fields to visual channels. The same names work for every chart type: `x` is category or time, `y` is the measured value(s). Switching `type` between line, bar, donut, stacked-area, or combo needs no re-encoding. Each channel is a field name string, or `{ field, type?, title?, format?, scale? }`.
description: `encoding` binds data fields to visual channels. The same names work for every chart type: `x` is category or time, `y` is the measured value(s). Switching `type` between line, bar

sections.title: Channels
paragraphs: From `$defs/encoding`. Only set the channels your mark needs — line/bar want `x`+`y`; scatter may add `size`/`color`; candlestick uses `open`/`high`/`low`/`close`/`volume`.
code: `encoding.x // category or time (donut: slice; heatmap calendar: date) encoding.y // measured value(s) — one field, or y[] for wide multi-series encoding.series // long data: split rows by this field (not with y[]) encoding.color // field, or { value } constant; heatmap: value field encoding.size // scatter bubble radius field encoding.open | high | low | close | volume // candlestick`

sections.title: Shorthand vs object
paragraphs: A plain string is the field name. Expand to an object when you need measurement type, title, format, or scale. Type is inferred when omitted: numbers → quantitative, ISO dates / epoch ms on x → temporal, other strings → nominal.
code: `// shorthand "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "signups" } // full channel "encoding": { "x": { "field": "week", "type": "ordinal", "title": "Week" }, "y": { "field": "signups", "type": "quantitative", "format": "compact", "title": "Signups" } }`

sections.title: Try a channel focus
paragraphs: Edit the JSON or flip Type / Theme / Focus (x·y · wide · series · color · size). The response path names the encoding branch. The mock chart still draws the Overview area; Focus only labels the channel story.

sections.title: Wide `y[]` vs long `series`
paragraphs: Multi-series data comes in two shapes. Wide: one column per series — `encoding.y` is an array of fields (or yChannel objects). Long: one value column plus a splitter — set `encoding.series` to that field. Do not combine `encoding.series` with an array `encoding.y` (CK2006).
y extras: on a yChannel object you can set `mark` (combo: line|bar|area), `axis: "y"|"y2"`, `color`, `dash`, and `area` (fill under a line).
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "trial": 18, "paid": 8 }, { "week": "W2", "trial": 28, "paid": 12 }, { "week": "W3", "trial": 24, "paid": 14 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": [ { "field": "trial", "title": "Trial" }, { "field": "paid", "title": "Paid", "dash": "dashed" } ] }, "a11y": { "alt": "Trial and paid signups by week." } }`

`{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "plan": "trial", "n": 18 }, { "week": "W1", "plan": "paid", "n": 8 }, { "week": "W2", "plan": "trial", "n": 28 }, { "week": "W2", "plan": "paid", "n": 12 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "n", "series": "plan" }, "a11y": { "alt": "Trial and paid signups by week." } }`

sections.title: Color & size
paragraphs: `encoding.color` accepts a field (categorical or sequential), a full colorChannel with optional `range`, or `{ "value": "#0071e3" }` for a constant. Heatmaps use color for the value field. `encoding.size` is scatter-only — bubble radius; object form may set `range: [min, max]` px (default `[3, 24]`).
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "scatter", "data": [ { "x": 12, "y": 40, "users": 120, "plan": "trial" }, { "x": 28, "y": 62, "users": 340, "plan": "paid" }, { "x": 44, "y": 55, "users": 210, "plan": "trial" } ], "encoding": { "x": "x", "y": "y", "size": { "field": "users", "range": [4, 28] }, "color": "plan" }, "a11y": { "alt": "Scatter of engagement by plan; bubble size is users." } }`

sections.title: Candlestick: OHLC (+ volume)
paragraphs: Candlestick does not invent a magic row shape — it uses explicit channels: `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, and optional `volume` (draws a volume pane when present). `x` is still the time field.
code: `"encoding": { "x": "date", "open": "o", "high": "h", "low": "l", "close": "c", "volume": "vol" }`

sections.title: One vocabulary, switch type
paragraphs: Legacy prop names (`dataKey`, `categoryKey`, `timeKey`, `xKey`/`yKey`, `sizeKey`, …) all fold into `encoding`. Change `"type": "line"` → `"bar"` or `"donut"` without renaming fields — donut uses `x` for the slice category and `y` for the value.
For agents

Emit `encoding.x` + `encoding.y` (or metric). Prefer shorthand strings. Use `y[]` or `series`, never both. Match field names to data keys. Then `validate()` — apply CK2001 fixes when a field is missing.
list: Field names in encoding must match `data` keys (or column names) — mismatch → CK2001.
Quantitative channels need numbers — non-numeric → CK2002.
Date-looking strings with the wrong type warn CK2003 (prefer `type: "temporal"`).
`scale` lives on the channel (data mapping). Axes are display only — see Scales next.

sections.title: Next
paragraphs: Scales sit on the channel (`encoding.*.scale`) — domain, log/sqrt/time/band, zero, nice, reverse. Axes only control ticks and labels.

title: Scales
lede: A scale maps data values to positions (or sizes). It lives on the channel — `encoding.x.scale` / `encoding.y.scale` — not on the axis. Axes are display only (title, ticks, format). Usually inferred from the field’s measurement type; set `scale` only to override.
description: A scale maps data values to positions (or sizes). It lives on the channel — `encoding.x.scale` / `encoding.y.scale` — not on the axis. Axes are display only (title, ticks, format).

sections.title: On the channel
paragraphs: From `$defs/scale`. Attach under any full channel object (`x`, `y`, `color`, `size`, …). Shorthand field strings have no place for scale — expand to `{ "field", "scale" }` when you need an override.
code: `"encoding": { "x": "week", "y": { "field": "signups", "scale": { "type": "linear", "domain": [0, 100], "zero": true, "nice": true, "reverse": false } } }`

sections.title: scale.type
paragraphs: Enum: `linear`, `log`, `sqrt`, `time`, `band`, `point`. Inferred from field type when omitted: quantitative → linear, temporal → time, nominal/ordinal → band. Legacy `xScaleType` / `yScaleType` map here.
list: `log` needs strictly positive values — zeros or negatives → CK3001 (use `sqrt`, filter, or offset).
`band` / `point` for categories; `domain` can list the ordered categories.
`time` pairs with temporal fields (ISO strings or epoch ms).

sections.title: Try a scale focus
paragraphs: Edit the JSON or flip Type / Theme / Focus (infer · domain · log · zero · reverse). The response path names the scale option. The mock chart still draws the Overview area; Focus only labels the scale story.

sections.title: domain
paragraphs: Explicit `[min, max]` for continuous scales, or an ordered list of categories for band/point. Use `null` on one side to keep that end automatic — e.g. `[0, null]` pins the floor. Legacy axis `min`/`max` belong here as `encoding.y.scale.domain`, not on `axes.y`.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }, { "week": "W2", "signups": 28 }, { "week": "W3", "signups": 42 }, { "week": "W4", "signups": 86 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": { "field": "signups", "scale": { "domain": [0, 100] } } }, "a11y": { "alt": "Weekly signups on a 0–100 scale." } }`

sections.title: zero · nice · reverse
list: `zero` — force the domain to include 0. Default true for bar/area, false for line/scatter.
`nice` — round the domain to tidy tick values. Default true.
`reverse` — flip the direction of the scale (high at the bottom / left).
code: `"encoding": { "x": { "field": "date", "type": "temporal" }, "y": { "field": "price", "scale": { "zero": false, "nice": true } } }`

sections.title: log & sqrt
paragraphs: Use `"type": "log"` for orders of magnitude, `"sqrt"` when you want compression without forbidding zero. Log with any value ≤ 0 fails validation (CK3001) — prefer sqrt, filter non-positive rows, or offset the data.
code: `"encoding": { "x": "week", "y": { "field": "bytes", "type": "quantitative", "format": "bytes", "scale": { "type": "log" } } }`

sections.title: About `range`
paragraphs: `$defs/scale` does not take a `range` property. Output ranges live on the channel that needs them:
Position scales map into the plot area automatically; you pin extents with `domain`, not a pixel range.
list: `encoding.color.range` — colors in order (categorical) or low→high (sequential).
`encoding.size.range` — `[min, max]` point radius in px (default `[3, 24]`).

sections.title: Scales vs axes
paragraphs: Scale = data mapping (domain, type, zero…). Axis = chrome (title, tick count, label format). Putting min/max on the axis is a legacy habit — in v1 they belong on `encoding.*.scale.domain`. See Axes next.
For agents
Omit `scale` unless you need a fixed domain, log/sqrt, or `zero: false` on a line. Never put min/max on `axes`. After setting `type: "log"`, validate — apply CK3001 fixes if values ≤ 0.

title: Axes
lede: `axes` is display-only chrome: titles, tick count, label format, grid, and side. Scale domains and scale type live on `encoding.<channel>.scale` — not here. Each of `axes.x`, `axes.y`, and `axes.y2` may be `false` (hide), `true` (defaults), or an options object.
description: `axes` is display-only chrome: titles, tick count, label format, grid, and side. Scale domains and scale type live on `encoding.<channel>.scale` — not here. Each of `axes.x`, `axes

sections.title: Shape
paragraphs: From `$defs/axes`. Defaults: x bottom, y left, y2 right. Title defaults to the channel title (none for time axes). Format defaults to the channel format.
code: `"axes": { "x": { "title": "Week", "ticks": 8, "grid": false }, "y": { "title": "Signups", "format": "compact", "ticks": 5, "grid": "dashed", "labels": true, "position": "left" } }`

sections.title: Options
paragraphs: There is no `rotate` (or min/max) on `axes`. Domain and scale type stay on the channel; label crowding is handled by tick count and format, not a rotate flag.
list: `title` — axis title string.
`format` — tick label format (preset or format object); same vocabulary as channel `format`.
`ticks` — approximate tick count (integer 0–50).
`grid` — `true`/`false`, or `"solid"` | `"dashed"` | `"dotted"`.
`labels` — show tick labels (default `true`).
`position` — `top` | `bottom` | `left` | `right`.

sections.title: Try an axes focus
paragraphs: Edit the JSON or flip Type / Theme / Focus (defaults · title · ticks · grid · hide · y2). The response path names the axes branch. The mock chart still draws the Overview area; Focus only labels the axes story.

sections.title: Hide an axis
paragraphs: Set the key to `false` to remove that axis entirely. `true` is explicit defaults (same as omitting the key for most charts).
code: `"axes": { "x": false, "y": { "grid": true, "ticks": 4 } }`

sections.title: Grid
paragraphs: Grid lines are drawn from the axis you configure. Boolean on/off, or a dash style. Legacy `showGrid` / `grid.horizontal` map to `axes.y.grid` and `axes.x.grid`.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }, { "week": "W2", "signups": 28 }, { "week": "W3", "signups": 42 }, { "week": "W4", "signups": 86 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "signups" }, "axes": { "x": { "grid": false, "title": "Week" }, "y": { "grid": "dotted", "format": "compact", "title": "Signups" } }, "a11y": { "alt": "Weekly signups with a dotted y grid." } }`

sections.title: Second axis (`y2`)
paragraphs: `axes.y2` is the right-hand axis for series with `encoding.y[].axis: "y2"` (combo / dual-scale lines). Configuring `axes.y2` with no y series on y2 — or the reverse — is CK3002.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "combo", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "signups": 18, "revenue": 2400 }, { "week": "W2", "signups": 28, "revenue": 3100 }, { "week": "W3", "signups": 42, "revenue": 4800 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": [ { "field": "signups", "mark": "bar", "title": "Signups" }, { "field": "revenue", "mark": "line", "axis": "y2", "title": "Revenue" } ] }, "axes": { "y": { "title": "Signups" }, "y2": { "title": "Revenue", "format": "currency", "position": "right" } }, "a11y": { "alt": "Signups as bars and revenue on a right axis." } }`

sections.title: Axes vs scales
paragraphs: Legacy `yAxisLeft={{ min, max, tickCount, format }}` splits in v1: `min`/`max` → `encoding.y.scale.domain`; `tickCount`/`format`/`unit`-as-title → `axes.y`. Labels `xLabel` / `yLabel` / `yLabelRight` → `axes.x.title` / `axes.y.title` / `axes.y2.title`.
For agents
Set titles, ticks, format, and grid on `axes`. Put min/max and log/linear on `encoding.*.scale`. If you add `axes.y2`, also set `axis: "y2"` on a y series (or drop y2) — then `validate()`.

sections.title: Next
paragraphs: Themes & tokens set colors, surfaces, and series palettes. Axis and grid strokes pick up theme tokens (`axis`, `grid`, `muted`) unless you override elsewhere.

title: Themes & tokens
lede: `theme` sets look and feel: a preset name (17 + `auto`), or `{ preset, mode, tokens }`. Theme by tokens, not hex — every token is also read from CSS variables `--ck-<token>` and `--ck-series-N` on the container, so a host design system can style charts with no JS. Default `"auto"`.
description: `theme` sets look and feel: a preset name (17 + `auto`), or `{ preset, mode, tokens }`. Theme by tokens, not hex — every token is also read from CSS variables `--ck-<token>` and `-

sections.title: Presets
paragraphs: From `$defs/theme` / `themes.ts`. Dark (13): `midnight`, `emerald`, `mono`, `slate`, `arctic`, `orchid`, `obsidian`, `neon`, `mocha`, `owl`, `retro`, `copper`, `rose`. Light (4): `sunset`, `silver`, `pearl`, `latte`. Plus `auto` — follows host CSS variables and `prefers-color-scheme`.

Docs shell note: the try-it Theme chips use Soft and Midnight. `midnight` is a shipped dark preset. Soft is the mock docs accent (not in the schema enum) — swap to a real preset name in production specs.
code: `{ "version": "1", "type": "line", "data": [ { "week": "W1", "signups": 18 }, { "week": "W2", "signups": 28 }, { "week": "W3", "signups": 42 }, { "week": "W4", "signups": 86 } ], "encoding": { "x": "week", "y": "signups" }, "theme": "midnight", "a11y": { "alt": "Weekly signups on midnight." } }`

sections.title: Try Soft ↔ Midnight
paragraphs: Flip the Theme chips (already in the Overview shell) — Soft vs Midnight. Use Focus to label preset · tokens · mode · CSS · series. The response path tracks the theme story; the chart recolors with the chip.

sections.title: Object form: preset · mode · tokens
paragraphs: Use the object when you need light/dark force or token overrides on top of a base preset.
list: `mode`: `auto` (default) | `light` | `dark` — force or follow `prefers-color-scheme`.
In React, `useAutoTheme({ light: "sunset", dark: "midnight" })` picks a preset from the host scheme.
code: `"theme": { "preset": "midnight", "mode": "dark", "tokens": { "accent": "var(--brand)", "series": ["#5ac8fa", "#34c759", "#ff9f0a"] } }`

sections.title: Token keys
paragraphs: Override individually under `theme.tokens`. Values are CSS colors or `var(--x)`.
Legacy per-mark colors (`upColor`, `downColor`, `trackColor`, …) fold into these tokens or `encoding.color`.
code: `background // chart background surface // card / tooltip text // primary text muted // secondary text, tick labels grid // grid lines axis // axis lines accent // single-series default highlight positive // good / up (deltas, up candles) negative // bad / down fontFamily // CSS font-family fontSize // base size in px (6–32) series[] // categorical palette (1–24 colors)`

sections.title: CSS variables `--ck-*`
paragraphs: Resolution order: CSS custom properties on the chart container, then token overrides, then the preset. Set host variables once — charts inherit with no re-render for dark mode.
shadcn / Tailwind: map `--chart-1..5` into `--ck-series-N` and `--ck-accent`. With `theme: "auto"`, the chart follows the host without a preset name.
code: `.app { --ck-background: canvas; --ck-surface: var(--card); --ck-text: var(--foreground); --ck-muted: var(--muted-foreground); --ck-grid: color-mix(in oklab, var(--border) 80%, transparent); --ck-axis: var(--border); --ck-accent: var(--chart-1); --ck-positive: var(--chart-2); --ck-negative: var(--destructive); --ck-series-1: var(--chart-1); --ck-series-2: var(--chart-2); --ck-series-3: var(--chart-3); /* … through --ck-series-12 */ }`

sections.title: Series palette
paragraphs: `tokens.series` is the categorical order. Default falls back to `var(--ck-series-1..12)`, then the preset. Too many series for the palette warns CK4002 — shorten groups or extend `series`. Text contrast below WCAG AA warns CK4004 on the offending token.
For agents

sections.title: Validate → repair → render
paragraphs: Point at `llms.txt`, emit a spec, then `validate()`. On failure, `repair()` applies JSON Patch locally. Then `render()` (or SSR `renderToString`). This page is step 1.
For agents
`ok: true` means zero errors (warnings allowed). Every diagnostic carries a stable `code`, a JSON Pointer `path`, optional `hint`, and often a `fix` patch for `repair()`.

sections.title: validate()
paragraphs: `validate(spec, data?)` runs structural checks from the v1 JSON Schema plus data-aware field, scale, and design diagnostics. A string is parsed as JSON first (`CK1001` on failure). All diagnostics return in one pass — sorted with repairable codes first.
code: `import { validate } from "@chartkitdev/core/validate"; const result = validate(spec); // result.ok · result.errors · result.warnings · result.diagnostics if (!result.ok) { for (const d of result.errors) { console.log(d.code, d.path, d.message); // d.hint · d.fix (RFC 6902 JSON Patch ops) } }`

sections.title: Diagnostic shape
paragraphs: Codes are stable (`CK1xxx` structure, `CK2xxx` data, `CK3xxx` semantics, `CK4xxx` design). Messages may improve; codes do not. Browse the full catalog on Errors.
code: `type Diagnostic = { code: string; // e.g. "CK2001" severity: "error" | "warning"; message: string; path: string; // JSON Pointer; "" = root hint?: string; fix?: JsonPatchOperation[]; // RFC 6902 — for repair() };`

sections.title: JSON Pointer
paragraphs: Each diagnostic `path` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the spec (e.g. `/encoding/y/field`). Click a pointer in the try-it rail to highlight that key in the editor. Agents use the same path for `fix` ops — no fuzzy string surgery.

sections.title: Validate → repair → render
paragraphs: `repair()` lifts first-try failures without another model call. It only applies patches the validator already proposed — nothing invented beyond `fix`.
For agents
Playground diagnostics expose Apply fix (one patch) and Repair all (`repair()` loop). CK1001 invalid JSON has no `fix` — parse first. CK3012 warnings stay as accepted-not-applied.

sections.title: repair()
paragraphs: `repair(spec, data?)` clones the input, collects `fix` ops from current errors, applies them with `applyPatch`, revalidates, and repeats up to a few rounds. Stops when `ok`, when no patch applies, or when errors stop changing. Returns `RepairResult`: the repaired `spec`, `applied` patches, plus the usual `ok` / diagnostics.
code: `import { validate, repair } from "@chartkitdev/core/validate"; const before = validate(spec); if (!before.ok) { const after = repair(spec); // after.spec — patched clone (input not mutated) // after.applied — RFC 6902 ops that landed, in order // after.ok — revalidate result }`

sections.title: JSON Patch (RFC 6902)
paragraphs: Each diagnostic may carry `fix: JsonPatchOperation[]`. Agents can apply a single op (Apply fix) or run the full loop (Repair all). Ops use the same JSON Pointers as `path`.
code: { "op": "replace", "path": "/encoding/y/field", "value": "revenue" }
{ "op": "add", "path": "/a11y", "value": { "alt": "Monthly revenue" } }
{ "op": "replace", "path": "/type", "value": "donut" }

sections.title: RepairResult

Does not invent fields: only ops from diagnostic `fix` arrays. Paths already gone are skipped. Max rounds keep pathological loops from spinning.
code: `{ "ok": true, "spec": { /* patched clone */ }, "applied": [ { "op": "replace", "path": "/encoding/y/field", "value": "revenue" } ], "errors": [], "warnings": [], "diagnostics": [] }`

paragraphs: `render()` is the loop end. After validate/repair, agents draw once — no model call. Core returns an SVG string (or error SVG); adapters expose the same bytes as `renderToString`.
For agents

Ship the SVG string from `render`/`renderToString`. Playground can rasterize to PNG (2× canvas) and share via `/playground#<encodeURIComponent(spec)>`. Prefer validate → repair before render so agents don’t paint error SVGs.

sections.title: render()
paragraphs: `render(spec, target?)` looks up `spec.type` in the shared registry, draws SVG, and optionally writes `target.innerHTML`. It does not validate and does not throw on bad input — unknown types return an error SVG (`CK1010`). Import `@chartkitdev/core/all` (or register charts) before calling.

sections.title: renderToString
paragraphs: Adapters wrap the same core draw for SSR. Vanilla / React return the SVG string synchronously; Vue’s `@chartkitdev/vue/ssr` is async through `vue/server-renderer`. SvelteKit SSR includes the SVG from the component.
code: `import { renderToString } from "@chartkitdev/vanilla"; const svg = renderToString(spec); // = core render(spec) import { renderToString } from "@chartkitdev/vue/ssr"; const html = await renderToString(spec); // includes SVG`

sections.title: SVG · PNG
paragraphs: SVG is the source of truth from `render`. PNG is a client export — playground draws the SVG onto a 2× canvas and downloads `chartkit.png`. Agents that need pixels should keep the SVG and rasterize at the edge.
`image/svg+xml` blob from the returned string. Download as `chartkit.svg`. Works in SSR, email, and Markdown fences.
Rasterize current SVG at 2× via `canvas.toBlob`. Fills page `--bg` behind the chart. Not returned by core `render()`.
